title: Rapid Zoom In
description: A rapid zoom in snaps focal length faster than a polite crash, almost a cut, the world tightening in a few frames, then a hold. The camera body does not travel.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: No time for a dolly. Emphasis as a weapon: a face, a gun, a sign.
The snap is so short it can read as an axial cut with a trail of glass. A crash zoom is already fast; this is faster than a polite crash.
If you can feel a leisurely enlarge, it is not rapid. If the body moved, you dollied.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Locked sticks or a locked handheld brace, zoom thrown to the end stop in a fraction of a second, then hold. Wide to tight.
No parallax. Prompt: Rapid zoom in on [Subject], faster than a polite crash, almost a cut, the world snapping tight.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a fact must arrive as a snap, not a walk. Do not use it on every line.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Hot Fuzz weaponizes snap zooms as punctuation. Kill Bill uses snap zooms as comic and violent emphasis.
Grammar: almost a cut, then a hold.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a dolly-in or a slow crash. The tell: parallax, or a leisurely enlarge.
The fix: locked body, snap to tight in a few frames, hold.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Rapid Zoom In in film?
A rapid zoom in is an extremely fast optical snap into the subject, almost a cut, then a hold. The camera body stays put.
Rapid Zoom In vs Crash Zoom In
A crash zoom in is a fast but readable punch. Rapid zoom in is faster than a polite crash, nearer to a cut with a trail of glass.
When should I use Rapid Zoom In?
Use it when there is no time for a dolly and the fact must snap tight. Do not use it on every line.
How do I prompt Rapid Zoom In for AI image or video?
Write an extremely fast zoom, then a hold. Example: Rapid zoom in on [Subject], faster than a polite crash, almost a cut, the world snapping tight.
